newsitem.title: USA: Schwab has no plans to buy fund co.
newsitem.headline: Schwab has no plans to buy fund co.

text.p: ORLANDO, Fla., Nov 8, Reuter - Charles Schwab & Co Inc President David Pottruck said the company has no plans to buy any mutual fund firms.

"I don't think an acquisition is likely to happen," Pottruck said during an informal session with reporters at a Schwab conference here. "There are not that many fund companies that would make a difference to us."
There have been rumors that Schwab was in the market to buy a mutual fund company.
Pottruck said that a large number of fund firms are up for sale in today's market. "A lot of mutual fund companies get shopped," Pottruck said. "They usually call us to see if we're interested."
Schwab has made its presence felt in the business through its Mutual Fund Onesource program, a fund supermarket for individual investors,
Schwab has decided that the prices are too high, Pottruck said, adding that Schwab executives don't believe that owning a fund firm would fit the company's strategic plans.
Pottruck said he expects growth of 50 percent in revenues and assets in its overall international businesses.
"We're quite hopeful the growth will be tremendous," Pottruck said.
In October, Schwab hired Mark Collier as senior vice president and co-head of its international unit, overseeing all of its different businesses.
Last year, Schwab bought ShareLink Investment Services Plc, a U.K. firm, as a beachhead into international business.
He said the company is eager to develop its 401k business, and offshore business market.
